## Inherited from livespec
verdicts.rationale: The paragraph "A refused commit's needs-human cause is attributable from the ledger" requires the excerpt to be the first failing test id or, when none is reported, the output's first line that reports an error. It also requires the cause to state that the failing target is unknown, with the reason named, when the hook output names no failed target. A ruff finding line reports an error and a numbered source-context line does not, so all four bullets follow from that clause, even though it does not spell out the `<path>:<line>:<column>: <RULE>` line format.

The Claim tokens rule in contracts.md under this heading says "Token records MUST be excluded from `list-work-items`, `next`, `needs-attention`'s work-item facts and every child enumeration." That covers all four listing surfaces the tests check. The no-history record class is a choice of implementation, not something the spec states. Tests that fail when a token is minted as an ordinary issue verify the same MUST.

verdicts.rationale: The ratified text states a fix-loop cap with a "non-converged" exit edge routing back to the Dispatcher's `backlog` bounce, which is the exit the work item wants to reuse. It does not state the new trigger: leaving through that exit when a fix turn leaves the head unchanged and the next janitor visit fails again, or the bound of two no-progress fix turns before the wall budget. The text also does not say that a head-changing fix still routes to janitor.
